author: owned_io_architect
review: Roster4e5d2791f522e3ca verified; architect active; AGENTS, INIT, profile, plan4/5 and design read.
decision: Use small concrete descriptor helpers in the existing observer, each <=50 lines. No callback framework or dependency. Select BaseExceptionGroup and explicitly raise diagnostic minimum to Python3.11 in README. Guest3.12 and parent-confirmed host3.15 need no install; drop host3.10 support. Unsupported required POSIX flags/dir_fd/scandir(fd) fail closed.
directory: Validate absolute path encoded with os.fsencode: <=4096 bytes, <=64 components, no NUL, empty interior/trailing component, dot or dotdot. Open root then each single component via os.open(component, O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC, dir_fd=parent). Never pass an absolute child to dir_fd. Transfer final fd only on success. fstat final (st_dev,st_ino,st_uid,st_mode) must equal supplied trusted tuple; require directory type. Ancestors need not share final UID/mode.
file: Allowlist fixed single filenames and caps. os.open(name,O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC|O_NONBLOCK,dir_fd=owned_fd), then fstat requires regular file before read. O_NONBLOCK avoids FIFO open hanging before type rejection; it is no general IO deadline. Use unbuffered io.FileIO(fd,'rb',closefd=False) with read_bounded(cap), preserving sole raw-fd ownership even if wrapping fails. Close wrapper then raw fd; never return bytes before cleanup succeeds. Ignore proc st_size.
children: os.scandir(owned_cgroup_fd) borrows caller fd; separately close iterator on every exit. Stream entries, never list/sort. Inspect <=64 entries and one extra entry only to detect overflow. Fresh os.stat(entry.name,dir_fd=fd,follow_symlinks=False), reject any directory or symlink; any lookup error invalidates census. No recursive traversal. Iteration is not an atomic subtree snapshot.
process: Read cgroup.procs only through pinned cgroup fd and existing 4096-byte/64-PID parser. Open numeric PID directories relative to pinned proc root only for census PIDs. Bind PID-directory fstat tuple before/after existing process_snapshot fixed-file reads; retain stat PID/start and membership double checks. No proc scan or unrelated parent reads. Keep owned_unattributed.
cleanup: Each acquisition has exactly one owner. Relinquish ownership before exactly one close attempt; never retry failed Linux close, including EINTR. Attempt all remaining closes even after failure; retain bounded ordered exceptions. Return only without failures. Exactly one failure re-raises the identical exception. Multiple failures raise BaseExceptionGroup with original primary first if present, then cleanup errors in close-attempt order; retain nested groups. Catch BaseException only to guarantee cleanup and preserve KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit in the group. Do not mutate arbitrary exceptions or suppress failures. Caller must handle groups and emit bounded typed reason/errno records, never raw repr. No fd double-close or success after cleanup error.
limits: Pinned fds prevent following replacement paths but do not prove current pathname or an atomic batch. At sampling/admission boundaries freshly repeat no-follow walk and compare pinned identity; also recheck fstat. Transient rename/ABA, membership movement and concurrent child creation can escape discrete checks. st_dev alone is not mount identity. Boot/container epoch, mount custody, expected UID/mode and trusted PID/cgroup binding remain native preflight obligations; No native authority.
essential: Host fault tests must cover component/final symlinks, renamed/replaced paths, bad tuples, FIFO, overflow, iterator errors, PID reuse and primary plus multiple cleanup failures. Keep source-only and null epoch until independent native preflight.
